name: Aembit
description: A workload access platform with X.509-SVID and JWT-SVID credential providers. It attests workloads, evaluates access policy, and supplies credentials for the destination service.

name: Akeyless
description: Provides SPIRE KeyManager and UpstreamAuthority plugins, plus a SecretManager plugin for storing issued X.509-SVIDs.

name: Anthropic / Claude
description: Exchanges JWT-SVIDs from a configured SPIFFE issuer for Claude API access tokens. Federation rules match workload claims and select a service account, workspace, and OAuth scope.

name: Cofide Connect
description: A workload identity platform built around SPIRE. It manages attestation policy and trust relationships, delivers SVIDs through the Workload API, and provides application integrations and workload events.

name: Defakto
description: A SPIFFE identity platform for workloads across Kubernetes, virtual machines, and serverless environments. Its documented integrations use SVIDs and trust domains to authenticate to services and exchange credentials with cloud platforms.

name: Edera
description: Runs SPIRE agents inside isolated zones, with an edera-hypervisor node attestor and delivery of workload credentials through files or a Workload API socket.
notes: The spire-v0 integration is disabled by default. Its current zone attestation identity is self-asserted and not yet hardened.

name: Eviden KMS (formerly Cosmian KMS)
description: Its Vault-compatible PKI endpoint signs SPIRE intermediate CA requests through the Vault UpstreamAuthority plugin. A native KMIP KeyManager integration stores signing keys and performs signing operations in the KMS.
notes: The Vault-compatible configuration uses AppRole for KMS access. SPIRE KeyManager PR #7235 merged on 2026-10-02; the KMIP plugin is absent from the latest tagged SPIRE release, v1.15.5, as of 2026-11-03.

name: Google Cloud managed workload identities
description: Google Cloud provisions SPIFFE-based X.509 credentials and trust anchors through Certificate Authority Service for supported Compute Engine and GKE workloads. Applications can use the credentials for mutual TLS. The documented GKE offering is in Preview. Available features and identity formats depend on the workload environment.

name: Greymatter
description: An application networking platform that integrates SPIRE to provision workload identities. Its service networking layer combines certificate-based mutual authentication with identity-aware traffic and access policies.

name: Idira Secure Workload Access
description: Palo Alto Networks' workload identity offering attests workloads and issues SPIFFE credentials. Its agents provide a local Workload API, with documented paths for secrets access and JWT-SVID credential exchange.

name: Kong Mesh
description: A commercial distribution of Kuma. MeshIdentity supports bundled SPIFFE certificate issuance and a SPIRE provider.

name: Messier 42 Quantum Helix
description: Kubernetes workload identity with TPM node attestation, namespace-selected authorities, and X.509-SVID delivery through the Workload API. QHx Notary signs identity-bound application records through AI and messaging middleware. CABE integration controls access to encrypted objects.

name: Microsoft Entra Workload ID
description: Exchanges SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs for Microsoft Entra access tokens through workload identity federation, using a configured issuer, subject, and audience.

name: OpenAI
description: Exchanges JWT-SVIDs from a configured SPIFFE issuer for OpenAI API access tokens. Claim mappings select a project service account and can narrow its API permissions.

name: Red Hat Zero Trust Workload Identity Manager
description: An OpenShift operator that manages SPIRE components and workload registration. It provides a supported product path for deploying SPIFFE identities and configuring federation in Red Hat environments. Feature maturity and support depend on the product release and OpenShift version; consult the matching release documentation.

name: Riptides
description: Issues X.509-SVIDs with SPIFFE IDs in URI SANs and JWT-SVIDs with SPIFFE IDs as subjects. A node daemon matches process selectors; a Linux kernel module generates X.509 private keys and requests certificates through the daemon and control plane. The module uses those credentials for transparent mutual TLS and applies connection policy.

name: StrongDM ID
description: An identity service that issues audience-scoped JWT-SVIDs through an authenticated HTTP API and publishes a trust bundle for verification. Its SPIFFE client examples cover Python, Go, and TypeScript.

name: Teleport Workload Identity
description: Teleport issues short-lived X.509-SVIDs and JWT-SVIDs from a cluster's workload identity authority. Its tbot agent can expose the SPIFFE Workload API and deliver credentials to applications and proxies.

name: Traefik Hub
description: A commercial API gateway that retrieves X.509-SVIDs from the Workload API to authenticate connections to backends.
